context_length.finding: LM Studio honoured the requested -c 65536 for the GGUF and for the Qwen3-Coder MLX build and ignored it for the Qwen3.8 and Qwen3.6 MLX builds, which loaded with 169728 (6-bit alias), 208384 (qwen/qwen3.8-27b 4-bit) and 262144 (qwen/qwen3.6-35b-a3b); see loaded_context_observed per candidate. The launcher therefore reads the loaded context from lms ps --json at preflight and refuses below 65536; it also checks the model key and the quantization of the loaded instance.

findings: No blocking issues. The diff touches only src/calc.py: mean() now uses true division and raises ValueError on empty input, which is exactly what tests/test_calc.py requires. Verified by running `python3 -m pytest -q`: 3 passed.
Scope is compliant with TASK.md: tests are unmodified, and no test configuration files, virtual environments or installed packages were added (git status shows only src/calc.py modified).

Non-blocking note: `if not values` raises an ambiguous-truth-value error for numpy arrays and treats an exhausted generator as non-empty (then fails in len()); irrelevant for the list inputs the tests and task cover.

cloud_findings.cloud_tool_set: Cloud arms have only the built-in tools Read, Edit, Write and Bash (init event, 29-name list). Bash itself is unrestricted except for the best-effort cloud_bash_deny rules (command-prefix permission rules, evadable); web, sub-agent and workflow TOOLS are absent, but a shell can still reach the network. The local harness omp exposes its own tool set (read, edit, write, bash, glob seen in the smoke runs): this asymmetry between arms is recorded, not equalised.
cloud_findings.sandbox: Under sandbox-exec Claude Code could not authenticate: with the keychain read-denied it said 'Not logged in'; with the keychain allowed it got '401 OAuth access token has been revoked', after which the maintainer had to log in again in a terminal (cause not established; possibly the sandboxed or TMPDIR-overridden child). Decision: cloud drivers run WITHOUT sandbox-exec (sandbox: false with this reason), with the AGENTS.md R6 environment intact (HOME, LANG, LC_ALL, LOGNAME, PATH, TMPDIR, USER, the real TMPDIR) and the disposable bundle as working directory.
cloud_findings.session_log_layout: premium_tokens(session_id) read from <projects>/*/<session_id>.jsonl equals the host's own result.usage exactly for the three runs (input, cache read, cache write, output). Only one file named by the session id existed each time. layout_verified is set to true CONDITIONALLY on the launcher asserting from the stream's system/init event that no sub-agent tool (Agent, Task) is available.
cloud_findings.tool_set_assertion: The launcher refuses a cloud record unless the init event's tools are a subset of allowed_tools (Bash, Edit, Read, Write). The three smoke runs were made before this list existed (their init event listed Task among 25 tools); the allowlisted tool set below was observed at the init event only, with no model call.

cloud_findings.exposure: Cloud arms are bare Claude Code (--setting-sources project,local --strict-mcp-config: no Foundry plugin, hook or agent definition, so not the Eiffel/Maigret definitions and no R1 guard on gh pr merge / git push) with --permission-mode bypassPermissions, the real home, an open network and the user's implicit credentials (git credential helper through the keychain, gh configuration, ~/.config/foundry). The launcher applies no read denial to them. A cloud arm could read merged solutions (gh pr view, git clone, curl), act on the real repository through gh, start another claude -p whose tokens are never read, or exfiltrate. Mitigations are best-effort only: cloud_bash_deny permission rules, a post-run audit of commands and paths (contaminated records), and the bundle having no remote. The maintainer's explicit acceptance of this exposure is pending.

clean: the 3 final cloud runs (after the fix)
contamination_audit_real_streams.false_positive_before_fix: the Sonnet 5.5 run (3rd Bash call: a python heredoc editing src/calc.py with `return sum(values) / len(values)`) was flagged `/`: the division operator was read as the filesystem root, which contains the bundle. Reason for the fix: a token made only of slashes is not a path. Known limit: a bare `ls /` is no longer flagged (it reveals no file content); `/etc/x` or `~` still are.

limits: tokens of a neutral-harness run are unknown (no event stream)

an unsandboxed cloud arm has the real home, an open network, the user's implicit credentials and no Foundry hook: it can read anything the user can (plugin cache whose tests were merged before release 1.0.0, repositories), call gh/curl/git, or start another agent; the launcher applies best-effort Bash deny rules and audits the arm's commands and paths after the run (contaminated records) instead of preventing it
the weights digests are recorded here and are not recomputed by the launcher
one toy task per driver: a trial proves the command works, it measures no quality
a bare `ls /` (a token made only of slashes) is not flagged by the contamination audit: it reveals no file content, and the division operator of code must not make an honest run contaminated
